battle.name: 1805年埃及革命
battle.brief: 一八〇五年三月，開羅馬穆魯克貝伊在法國人撐腰下起兵反抗奧斯曼總督，帝國大軍與艦隊南下圍城，拉鋸在開羅城牆與尼羅河三角洲之間，最後以談判收場，穆罕默德·阿里出任埃及瓦利。火繩槍這類老式長槍仍留在上埃及民兵手上，英法運來的燧發步槍才是戰場主流。

kit.name: 火繩槍銃
kit.history: 比步槍輕的長槍。西班牙人帶著它上船，也帶著它進了美洲。

countries: 交戰的兩方，一邊是奧斯曼帝國的埃及總督區，一邊是開羅的馬穆魯克「家族」勢力，外加法英兩股伸進來的外部力量。奧斯曼一方以伊斯坦布爾的中央政府為骨幹：蘇丹塞利姆三世的樞密院與軍械庫、隨軍南下的卡普奇禁軍（耶尼切里與各鎮禁軍）、按新制法組訓的新式步兵（尼扎姆-傑迪德）、埃及總督區的土軍與省民兵（賽門），以及由卡普丹帕夏率領的帝國海軍。開羅的總督職位名義上凌駕於馬穆魯克之上，但稅收徵解、官員任免與兵權三樣東西長期被三方拉扯。馬穆魯克一方是十二位貝伊與各家家臣組成的武裝團體，核心是重裝騎兵（薩拉比斯特）、上埃及的阿拉伯火槍步兵與城門前的火砲隊；開羅的烏里瑪（宗教學者）與城民站在他們一邊，其中以阿里貝伊為首的那一支最具行動力。法國以駐埃及領事杜羅維蒂為核心，派出軍事顧問並以地中海分艦隊公開掩護馬穆魯克。英國則在蘇丹與法國之間兩面下注：駐埃及領事館以「埃及基金」名義代收稅款、發放馬穆魯克薪餉，皇家海軍地中海分隊在埃及外海巡弋，名義上仍是蘇丹的盟友，實際上先把法國人擋在尼羅河口以外。
countriesEn: The two sides were the Ottoman eyalet of Egypt and the Mamluk household of Cairo, with France and Britain reaching in from outside. On the Ottoman side stood the central government at Istanbul: the sultan's divan and arsenal, the Kapıkulu regulars (the Janissaries and the household troops of the provinces) marching with the relief army, the newly raised Western-drilled infantry of the Nizam-i Cedid, the Turkish troops and provincial levies (seymen) of the Egyptian province, and the imperial fleet under the Kapudan Pasha. The governorship of Cairo was nominally above the Mamluks, yet the collection of taxes, the appointment of officials and the right to bear arms were pulled three ways for decades. The Mamluk side was the armed following of twelve beys and their households: at its core the heavy cavalry (the sarabist), the musket infantry of Upper Egypt and the artillery parks before the gates of Cairo; the ulema and the townsmen of Cairo stood with them, and the faction headed by Ali Bey was the one most ready to act. France, through its consul-general Drovetti, sent military advisers and openly shielded the Mamluks with a squadron of the Mediterranean fleet. Britain played both sides against the middle: its consuls in Egypt received the tax revenues under the name of the Egyptian Fund and paid the Mamluk salaries, while the Royal Navy's Mediterranean detachment cruised off the Egyptian coast, an ally of the sultan in name that kept the French beyond the Nile mouth in fact.
people: 決定這場戰爭走向的是四個人和一群人。第一位是馬穆魯克家族之首阿里貝伊，他手握重騎兵，控制開羅的軍械與徵召，藉法國人撐腰，最後把自己推到與蘇丹分庭抗禮的位置上。第二位是艾哈邁德阿加，他與阿里貝伊同屬最不服蘇丹的貝伊，負責把馬穆魯克的火槍與砲隊編入作戰序列。第三位是奧馬爾阿加一系，較願意與英國人合作、倚靠英國的補貼，成了馬穆魯克陣營內主張妥協的一端。第四位是穆罕默德·阿里，這位阿爾巴尼亞出身的禁軍軍官原本奉命平叛，卻在攻陷開羅後被蘇丹任命為埃及瓦利，成為整場危機最大的受益者。蘇丹塞利姆三世在伊斯坦布爾遙控，但戰場指揮交給卡普丹帕夏，他帶著艦隊與大軍南下；同時海軍在亞歷山大外海有過一場交鋒，參戰雙方的旗艦名與序列在各方記載中互有出入，諸說並存，詳情難辨。杜羅維蒂是馬穆魯克背後的法國推手，替他們爭取顧問、船隻與外交支持；英國領事館與英軍顧問團則在另一邊替馬穆魯克付薪、發武器，同時把法國人釘在亞歷山大港以外。
peopleEn: Four men and one body of men decided how the war went. First was Ali Bey al-Kabir, head of the Mamluk household, who held the heavy cavalry, controlled the arms of Cairo and the calling up of the men, and leaned on the French until he found himself set against the sultan. Second was Ahmad Agha al-Safi, a bey as unwilling to accept the sultan's authority as Ali Bey, who brought the Mamluk muskets and guns into the order of battle. Third was the party of Omar Agha, more willing to work with the British and to live on British subsidies, which was the moderate edge inside the Mamluk camp. Fourth was Muhammad Ali, the Albanian janissary officer sent to put down the revolt, who ended up appointed wali of Egypt after the storming of Cairo and became the great beneficiary of the crisis. Selim III directed events from Istanbul, but the field command passed to the Kapudan Pasha, who brought the fleet and a great army south; at the same time a naval action was fought off Alexandria, though the flagship names and the order of battle of the two squadrons differ from account to account and the details remain contested. Drovetti was the French hand behind the Mamluks, winning them advisers, ships and diplomatic cover; the British consulates and their military advisers paid the salaries, supplied the weapons and pinned the French outside Alexandria at the same time.
kits: 任務單上的火繩槍銃，即十六世紀西班牙的 arquebus，在一八〇五年的埃及屬於一種過時但仍未絕跡的長槍。它的位置可以從三個層面看。第一，它已經是軍械庫裡的舊式樣：火繩機制在歐洲自十七世紀起被燧發槍取代，埃及總督區的武器來源又以奧斯曼本國與法國訂購為主，火繩槍只餘省級兵站與地方徵召在用，各級火槍隊普遍改持燧發的卡拉德長槍，射程與射速都勝一籌。第二，它仍留在次要部隊手上：上埃及的阿拉伯步兵、部分貝伊的私兵與鄉村武裝，火繩槍仍是主要長槍，價廉、耐用，對付缺乏防護的對手足夠。第三，它象徵著這支軍隊的混合性：馬穆魯克重騎兵用標槍、彎刀與短手槍，開火之後仍以標槍衝鋒；英國人替他們運來的是燧發步槍；法國人則帶來四磅與六磅輕炮和歐式操典。火砲方面，埃及師旅用四、六、八、十二磅滑膛銅炮，另有上埃及的長管獅子炮（jezail）與各砲隊的附屬火槍手；後勤靠尼羅河的帆船、船工與駱駝、驢子的馱運，砲隊缺新式步槍時以火繩槍改裝替代的做法，見於零星記載。
kitsEn: The kit on the card, the arquebus, the Spanish matchlock long gun of the sixteenth century, was by 1805 an outdated but not yet extinct arm in Egypt. Its standing can be read on three levels. First, it had become an old pattern in the arsenals: the matchlock had been replaced by the flintlock in Europe from the seventeenth century onward, and Egyptian procurement ran mainly on Ottoman and French sources, so the arquebus survived only in provincial depots and among locally raised men, while the regular musket corps carried flintlock muskets with better range and rate of fire. Second, it was still in the hands of the less regular troops: the Arab musketeers of Upper Egypt, the private retainers of individual beys and the village levies still used matchlocks, cheap, serviceable and good enough against poorly protected opponents. Third, it marks how mixed this army was: the Mamluk heavy cavalry carried lance, sabre and short pistols, firing before the charge; the British supplied flintlock muskets; the French brought four- and six-pounder light guns and the European drill. On the artillery side the Egyptian corps used four-, six-, eight- and twelve-pounder smoothbore bronze pieces, alongside the long-barrelled jezail and the musketeers attached to each gun; in the rear the Nile's sailing craft, the boatmen and the camel and donkey trains carried everything, and gun teams short of proper muskets were sometimes seen making do with converted arquebuses, a practice noted only in scattered records.
tactics: 馬穆魯克一方的打法以騎兵為主，攻城與野戰都圍繞開羅與三角洲。馬穆魯克重騎兵在會戰中排成楔形（努卡達），先以火槍或手槍齊射，再挾標槍與彎刀衝鋒，衝散之後各自迴旋重整，這是自十五世紀沿用下來的套路；近年因為英法顧問介入，才開始出現以刺刀線列步兵配合火砲射擊的歐式戰法。守城方利用開羅城牆、城堡與清真寺高台，在尼羅河與各運河的渡口設卡，阻止帝國軍糧船入城；圍城期間馬穆魯克多次夜襲包圍陣地，破壞攻城砲位與糧車。卡普丹帕夏的帝國軍則以海軍封鎖沿岸、以分隊佔領三角洲要道、逐步壓縮城內糧水，同時以砲兵隔河轟擊，把圍城拖成一場耐力戰。奧斯曼軍最大的弱點是人數眾多而補給線越拉越長：從伊斯坦布爾南下要走陸路，進三角洲後靠尼羅河運糧，夏季痢疾與熱病在營中迅速蔓延，多數說法都提到圍城軍因疫病而自行崩解。戰局真正轉折在法英的介入：法國想借馬穆魯克的手重返埃及，英國想保住自己的印度航路，雙方都把這裡當棋盤。一八〇七年英國以海軍掩護馬穆魯克聯軍登陸、攻入亞歷山大，再沿海岸向三角洲推進，但糧秣靠海船、進攻靠陸軍，兩者脫節，最終聯軍在夏季熱病與穆罕默德·阿里的反擊下退回地中海，戰事不了了之。
tacticsEn: The Mamluk side fought mounted, and both the siege and the field fighting turned on Cairo and the Delta. The heavy cavalry went in in wedge (nakda), volleying with musket or pistol before falling back on the lance and sabre, then wheeling and re-forming; that was a pattern inherited from the fifteenth century. Only in recent years, with French and British advisers present, did infantry in bayonet line working with field guns appear in European fashion. The defenders used the walls, the citadel and the raised platforms of the mosques, and set posts at the crossings of the Nile and the canals so that the imperial grain boats could not reach the city; during the siege the Mamluks broke out at night to destroy the batteries and the baggage trains. The Kapudan Pasha's army blockaded the coast with the fleet, held the roads of the Delta and squeezed the food and water of the city step by step, while the batteries shelled across the river, turning the siege into a test of endurance. The empire's real weakness was numbers against a lengthening line of supply: the march from Istanbul was made overland, and once in the Delta the grain came by the Nile; in summer dysentery and fever ran through the camp, and most accounts hold that the besieging army dissolved under disease. The real turning point was the intervention of France and Britain, each using Egypt as a board: France wanted the Mamluks to open the door back, Britain wanted to keep its road to India, and each wanted the other kept out. In 1807 Britain landed the Mamluk coalition under naval cover, took Alexandria and pushed along the coast into the Delta, but supply came by sea and the advance by land, and the two came apart; under the summer fevers and Muhammad Ali's counter-stroke the coalition fell back into the Mediterranean and the campaign ended without decision.
data: 關於兵員與數目，史載多為概數，諸說並存，須慎用。馬穆魯克家族在開羅的貝伊按傳統為十二位；整個家族在十八世紀末到十九世紀初的全員，近代研究者常概數為一萬至三萬，較多採用兩萬上下的說法，其中能列名於各役的薩拉比斯特重騎兵仍以數千計。帝國方面的遠征大軍，卡普丹帕夏的水陸大軍常被形容為數萬之眾，含禁軍、新式步兵與賽門民兵，具體名冊未見完整保存。圍城的時序較可考：馬穆魯克起事在一八〇五年三月，四月至六月間帝國軍進逼開羅並展開圍城，同年六、七月間在亞歷山大外海另有法英分艦隊交火，戰事延續至夏末方以談判收束。地理上，開羅至亞歷山大直線約一百八十至二百公里；尼羅河自開羅向北分岔為羅塞塔與達曼胡爾兩支分流，中間夾著一整片三角洲。武器射程方面，火繩槍的有效射程常被記作一百至一百五十步，燧發槍可推得更遠；埃及師旅的火砲口徑多在四、六、八與十二磅之間。人口與賦稅方面，十九世紀初的埃及人口常被概數為三百萬上下，具體統計並不完整，馬穆魯克的薪餉則靠英國經手的埃及基金支付。
dataEn: On numbers the sources are largely general estimates, they disagree with one another, and they must be used with care. The Mamluk household in Cairo traditionally counted twelve beys; the full strength of the household in the late eighteenth and early nineteenth century is commonly put between ten and thirty thousand, with twenty thousand the figure most often used, of whom the sarabist heavy cavalry actually identifiable in the rolls still numbered only in the thousands. The imperial relief army under the Kapudan Pasha is usually described as tens of thousands, including the Janissaries, the new-style infantry and the seymen, with no complete muster surviving. The chronology is firmer: the Mamluk revolt began in March 1805, the imperial army closed on Cairo and opened the siege between April and June, a French and British action was fought off Alexandria in June or July, and the matter was settled by negotiation at the end of the summer. Geographically, Cairo to Alexandria is roughly a hundred and eighty to two hundred kilometres; the Nile divides at Cairo into the Rosetta and Damietta branches, with the whole Delta between them. On ranges, the arquebus is usually credited with a hundred to a hundred and fifty paces of effective fire, while the flintlock went further; Egyptian guns ran to four, six, eight and twelve pounds. On population and revenue, Egypt at the beginning of the nineteenth century is generally estimated at about three million, though the returns are incomplete, and the Mamluk salaries were paid out of the Egyptian Fund handled by the British.
cause: 直接引爆點在奧斯曼帝國本身。塞利姆三世自一八〇五年前後推動的新制（尼扎姆-傑迪德）打算用西式操典與新式制服重建軍隊，同時整頓稅收與地方官員，動作愈急，觸動的既得利益者愈多；埃及馬穆魯克貝伊最在意的三件事——軍火自由、新式軍官不進埃及、以及關稅與地稅的重新攤派——都在改革名單上。帝國連年戰敗與海軍實力萎縮，亦令開羅馬穆魯克自覺實力上升；而法國在拿破崙治下的中介與徵募網絡，使馬穆魯克相信法國人會替他們擋住蘇丹，英國的埃及基金則在背後替這場抗爭付帳，形成一個三方互相利用的局面。拿破崙在歐洲戰事吃緊的同時仍保留重取埃及的計劃，英國因此更不願見奧斯曼重新控制尼羅河。於是稅制、軍制、歐洲戰局三股力量疊在一起，把一場原本只是地方貝伊與總督之間的齷齬，推成波及全省的武裝起事。
causeEn: The spark lay in the Ottoman Empire itself. The Nizam-i Cedid that Selim III pushed forward from around 1805 meant to rebuild the army on European drill and new uniforms while reforming the revenue and the provincial administration; the faster it moved, the more vested interests it disturbed. The three things the Egyptian beys cared about most, the free use of arms, the exclusion of new-style officers from Egypt, and the reassessment of customs and land tax, all stood on that reform list. Imperial defeats and the shrinking Ottoman navy also convinced the Mamluk beys of Cairo that their own strength had grown, while the French network of agents and recruiters under Napoleon made them believe France would stand between them and the sultan, and Britain's Egyptian Fund paid for the resistance behind the scenes, producing a three-way bargain in which everyone used everyone. Napoleon, hard pressed in Europe, still kept a plan for retaking Egypt, and Britain had even less wish to see the Ottomans hold the Nile again. Taxation, military reform and the war in Europe thus piled one on top of another and turned what had been a quarrel between local beys and a governor into an armed rising across the province.
impact: 一八〇五年之後，埃及再也回不去舊秩序。馬穆魯克保住了貝伊的名位，卻失去了兵權的最後一塊磚：帝國以收繳火槍、分期處理砲隊為名，拆掉了馬穆魯克的武裝骨幹；穆罕默德·阿里則以新式軍隊為柱石，用一八〇七年開始的全國徵兵（尼扎姆-紀哈德）把兵源從馬穆魯克手裡轉到國家手上。這套以稅養兵、以兵備戰的財政軍事國家雛形，日後成為改革埃及其他奧斯曼邊疆的樣板，也正是歐洲觀察者所擔憂的源頭。英國在埃及的角色急轉直下：一八〇七年英軍撤走，英法在東地中海的角力重心轉到愛爾海與亞得里亞海，英國把埃及讓給蘇丹，換取蘇丹在對俄與對法問題上的合作。從更長的視角看，這場危機把埃及推上區域強權的位置：一八〇七年後穆罕默德·阿里逐步削弱馬穆魯克，一八一一年、一八一五年與一八一六年三次清洗最終除掉這個舊貴族階級；他隨後的對外擴張、對歐洲的戰爭，以及一八八二年英軍進入埃及的結局，都可以回溯到一八〇五年這場在開羅城內爆發、又在尼羅河邊收場的起義。
impactEn: After 1805 Egypt could never go back to the old order. The Mamluks kept their beyliks and lost the last of their military power: the empire, under the pretext of taking in their muskets and dealing with their guns piece by piece, dismantled the armed backbone of the household. Muhammad Ali built on the new-style regiments and used the general conscription that began in 1807, the nizam al-jihad, to move the man-power out of Mamluk hands and into the state's; this embryo of a fiscal-military state, taxes paying for an army and an army ready for war, became a model later imitated in the reform of Egypt and in other Ottoman borderlands, and it was exactly the thing European observers feared. Britain's position in Egypt then fell away quickly: with the British gone in 1807, the Anglo-French contest in the eastern Mediterranean shifted to the Ionian Sea and the Adriatic, and Britain handed Egypt back to the sultan in exchange for Ottoman cooperation against Russia and France. In the longer view the crisis lifted Egypt into the place of a regional power. After 1807 Muhammad Ali wore down the Mamluks step by step, and the killings of 1811, 1815 and 1816 finally removed the old military aristocracy; his later wars of expansion, his campaigns in Europe and the British landing of 1882 all trace back to a rising that broke out inside Cairo and ended by the Nile.
result: 收場是談判出來的，不是打垮出來的。帝國軍在開羅城下僵持到一八〇五年夏，奧斯曼內部既不願為埃及再耗兵，也不願讓法國人長期佔據亞歷山大港，最後由伊斯坦布爾下詔：穆罕默德·阿里出任埃及瓦利，馬穆魯克貝伊保留在三角洲各省的總督職，但必須按期交出火槍與砲隊、接受帝國方面的點驗，並照舊從英國經手的埃及基金領取薪餉。與此同時，法國分艦隊在亞歷山大外海失利後退出埃及水域，英國地中海分隊重新控制尼羅河口。表面上起事者得了他們要的職位，代價卻是兵權；馬穆魯克在一八〇六至一八〇七年再度起兵，得到英國海軍支援的聯軍一度攻入亞歷山大，卻在三角洲和夏季的熱病裡消耗殆盡，英軍於同年九月撤走，聯軍瓦解。真正的清算要到一八一一年之後：穆罕默德·阿里在開羅城門下逐一誅殺不肯降的貝伊，其家臣或被貶為奴、或被逐往努比亞與上埃及，這個延續了三百年的軍事貴族集團才告終局。
resultEn: It ended in negotiation, not in a decisive defeat. The imperial army stalemated before Cairo through the summer of 1805; the Porte was unwilling to spend more men on Egypt or to let the French hold Alexandria for long, and Constantinople finally issued the decree: Muhammad Ali was made wali of Egypt, the Mamluk beys kept their governorships in the Delta provinces but were to hand over their muskets and guns by instalments, submit to inspection, and go on drawing their salaries from the Egyptian Fund handled by the British. At the same time the French squadron, beaten off Alexandria, withdrew from Egyptian waters, and the British detachment regained command of the Nile mouth. On the surface the rebels got what they wanted; the price was military power. The Mamluks rose again in 1806 and 1807, and the coalition backed by the British fleet entered Alexandria, only to be worn down in the Delta and in the summer fevers, with the British withdrawing in September and the coalition falling apart. The real reckoning came after 1811: Muhammad Ali had the beys who would not submit killed one by one at the gates of Cairo, their households enslaved or driven into Nubia and Upper Egypt, and only then was the end of the three-hundred-year-old military aristocracy complete.
